text:
maya: Heads up — saw a big IOPS spike in eu-west3 last night around 02:05 and it coincided with a handful of GPU attach failures. Appears to be local NVMe saturation during the nightly cleanup window. anyone seeing this?

jon: saw the alert too. linking the grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west3/io?s=1754320000..1754324000

infra-bot: ALERT: region=eu-west3 device=/dev/nvme0n1 iops>threshold for 4m — triggered 02:04:12 — janitor-cronjob-2026-03-09

sam: yep — janitor and scrub ran at the same time. previous window drifted due to DST + cron drift, so they overlapped with our usual nightly batch attach.

reinhardt: overlap + high-concurrency attach is death for small local SSDs. we saw ~1200 concurrent fsyncs in the tail. that will queue up and cause attach timeouts iirc.

maya: how bad were the attach failures? ops-sre?

ops-sre: 4 GPU attach failures, autoscaler retried and recovered. impact: ~2m increased latency for a few pods, some retries pushed job windows. no customer-facing errors but it's a capacity hit.

ali: we should consider temporary throttling of janitor in eu-west3 while we fix schedule. simple knob: per-device IOPS cap on janitor. low risk and quick.

sam: proposed quick fixes: 1) shift janitor cron by 1h for eu-west3 2) add per-node token-bucket rate limit in janitor 3) stagger scrub vs janitor so they never run same window

jon: agree. can we do a canary? shift just the canary pool (gnode-canaary-eu-west3) first.

infra-bot: ROLLOUT_PLAN created: janitor-rate-limit-featureflag = true; canary group = gnode-canary-eu-west3

maya: example rate-limit config we can push quickly (kustomize patch):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: janitor-config
data:
  per_device_iops: "10"  # token-bucket refill 10 iops
  bucket_size: "50"
```

reinhardt: 10 iops might be low for some flows, but fine as a temporary mitigation. we can tune after canary.

ops-sre: ops plan: push rate-limit to canary at 03:30, monitor IOPS, attach latency, and GPU attach error rate. rollback on >1% attach failures.

sam: also scheduling note: our cronjob controller had a drift bug when upgrading k8s 1.26 -> 1.27. cron windows drift by ~30m if controller restarts during DST. opened ticket: K8S-CRON-DRIFT-112.

ali: long term: make janitor expiry window dynamic via load-aware scheduler (avoid runs when disk Io > X). that's a bit more work but will prevent future collisions.

jon: can we do a cheap improvement now — prefer quiet-hours scheduling with a randomized jitter per node? reduces probability of simultaneous peaks without complex scheduling.

maya: agreed. short-term: 1) enable per-device iops=10 on canary 03:30 2) shift eu-west3 janitor window by +45m 3) add 5m jitter to cronjobs cluster-wide 4) follow up with dynamic load-aware refactor (Q2).

ops-sre: I'll create the change in flagger and the rollout PR. monitoring dashboard updated with new thresholds. Will ping channel when canary is live. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: CHANGESET: janitor-config patched on gnode-canary-eu-west3 at 03:29:45 by ops-sre.

maya: thanks. everyone keep an eye on grafana for the next 6 hours. if we see residual hotspots we'll consider moving scrub to daytime maintenance with rate-limited fast-path for attaches.

sam: note for cost team — if we reduce scrub aggressiveness we might increase long-term wear and chance of reclamation. tradeoff between immediate availability vs slightly higher drive wear/cost. cc @finance (not in this thread). :money_with_wings:

reinhardt: we'll measure wear delta; small softening of scrub cadence has minimal wear impact vs the cost of failed GPU attaches.

ops-sre: canary live at 03:30. initial metrics look good — 60% drop in peak iops and attach latency back to baseline. will keep rolling for 2h then decide on region-wide flip.

maya: closing loop: if canary stays healthy flip to eu-west3 at 06:00, otherwise roll back. great catch y'all. :coffee:
